boards.title: Your First Weekend at John Brown University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A practical Friday-to-Sunday sequence for learning JBU’s campus, joining student life, and exploring two under-21-safe Siloam Springs destinations.

cards.title: Start at Walker Student Center
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · Find the orientation information desk
cards.notes: Begin at the orientation information desk, then locate Student Development on the first floor so you know where to return with questions.
cards.short_summary: Use JBU’s designated orientation help point to get situated before exploring campus.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU states that its Orientation Information Desk and Student Development Office are located in Walker Student Center.
cards.source_title: Orientation for On-Campus Undergraduates at John Brown University
cards.access_notes: The information desk is associated with Orientation; Student Development is on the first floor. Confirm event-specific availability in the current schedule.

cards.title: Join the Group on the Quad
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Follow the current Orientation schedule
cards.notes: Bring water and comfortable shoes, meet your assigned group, and use the Quad gathering to learn faces before the weekend branches out.
cards.short_summary: Make the central campus lawn your first social waypoint, using the official schedule for the actual program.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU’s campus map names The Quad, and JBU’s published Orientation materials place recurring group events such as the organizations fair there.
cards.access_notes: Orientation programming is schedule-dependent; consult the current Fall 2026 schedule rather than relying on the archived packet’s times.

cards.title: Share a First Dinner at Kresge
cards.subtitle: Friday dinner · Use a meal scan or posted individual pricing
cards.notes: Meet your hall, floor, commuter, or orientation group for dinner and check the serving window before walking over from your residence area.
cards.short_summary: Use the main dining hall as a low-planning place to reconnect with your group after arrival tasks.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU publishes weekend meal periods for Kresge Dining Hall, including Saturday and Sunday meals, and lists meal-scan plans and individual pricing.
cards.access_notes: Saturday service is listed from 9:30 a.m.–6:30 p.m. with meal breaks; Sunday service is listed from 9:30 a.m.–6:30 p.m. Verify academic-break changes.

cards.title: Learn the Library Before You Need It
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Locate study rooms and student support
cards.notes: Walk both floors, identify the printers and Writing Center, then note how study-room reservations work before your first assignments arrive.
cards.short_summary: A short library orientation now makes later study sessions easier to plan.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU identifies the library in the Learning Resource Center and documents study rooms, computers, printers, the Writing Center, and IT Help Desk.
cards.access_notes: JBU currently lists Saturday library hours as 10 a.m.–6 p.m. and Sunday hours as 2 p.m.–2 a.m. on its commuter-resources page; academic-break hours may differ.

cards.title: Trace Dogwood Trail
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · Learn the north side of campus
cards.notes: Follow the named trail only in daylight, keep to established walkways, and use the route to recognize the athletics and residence-side landmarks.
cards.short_summary: Turn a daylight walk into a low-pressure campus geography lesson.
cards.evidence_claim: The official JBU campus map labels Dogwood Trail on the north side of campus near Sager Creek and multiple athletics facilities.
cards.access_notes: Use the official campus map and remain on marked routes. The source does not publish separate trail hours or guarantee conditions.

cards.title: Try a Recreation Session at Walton
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Bring your current JBU ID
cards.notes: Choose one facility activity that matches your experience, bring your student ID, and review posted rules before entering a court, track, or pool area.
cards.short_summary: Use a first workout to learn the campus recreation facility and its entry routine.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU describes Walton Lifetime Health Complex as its campus fitness facility, and current facility policy accepts a current student JBU ID for admission.
cards.source_title: Walton Lifetime Health Complex Policies and Procedures
cards.access_notes: Current JBU students must present their JBU ID. Facility schedules vary, so check the linked facility-hours information before visiting.

cards.title: Put Siloam Springs in Context
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · 112 North Maxwell Street
cards.notes: Browse the permanent and rotating exhibits, then connect one display about the springs, local industry, or earlier residents to the town outside.
cards.short_summary: Add local history to the weekend without requiring an admission purchase.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum states that it presents permanent and rotating exhibits about Siloam Springs history and that admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m., according to the museum. Admission is free; optional donations are accepted.

cards.title: Take a Park Break at Bob Henry
cards.subtitle: Saturday late afternoon · 500 West Benton Street
cards.notes: Walk through the public park, choose a court or open recreation area that is available, and leave reserved pavilions to scheduled groups.
cards.short_summary: Use a named city park for an unstructured outdoor pause before returning to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Siloam Springs lists Bob Henry Park at 500 West Benton Street with basketball, tennis, sand volleyball, playground, skate-park, and restroom amenities.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor amenities are city facilities; pavilion use may require a reservation. Check posted park rules, closures, and court availability on arrival.

cards.title: Close Sunday at The Gathering
cards.subtitle: Sunday evening · Student-led worship in the Cathedral
cards.notes: Check the current chapel calendar, arrive early enough to choose a seat, and treat attendance as a chance to observe a recurring part of JBU life.
cards.short_summary: End the first weekend with JBU’s documented Sunday-night, student-led worship gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU documents The Gathering as a student-led worship experience held every Sunday night in the Cathedral of the Ozarks.
cards.access_notes: The source identifies Sunday-night recurrence but does not provide a current start time. Confirm the time and any calendar exception before attending.

cards.title: Finish Orientation with Big Games
cards.subtitle: Orientation weekend · Join your assigned team
cards.notes: Wear clothes suited to warm outdoor activity, follow event leaders, and participate at your comfort level while learning your larger orientation team.
cards.short_summary: Use JBU’s recurring team activity to close the weekend with the people in your orientation group.
cards.evidence_claim: JBU states that Big Games occurs at the beginning of fall Orientation and combines orientation groups into larger teams for activities and obstacles.
cards.source_title: Student Traditions & Activities at John Brown University
cards.access_notes: Big Games is limited to scheduled fall Orientation programming. Follow the current Orientation schedule and event staff’s safety directions.
